proposals.before: At the time Xu Shang was Minister of the Lesser Treasury and Shi Dan was Chamberlain for Attendants. The emperor brought Shang and Dan into court as grand counselors of the household, promoted Ban Bo to chief commandant of waters and parks, and had him serve as Palace Attendant together with the two Shi men; all held the salary rank of fully two thousand piculs.
proposals.after: At the time Xu Shang was Minister of the Lesser Treasury and Shi Dan was Chamberlain for Attendants. The emperor brought Shang and Dan into court as grand counselors of the household, promoted Ban Bo to chief commandant of waters and parks, and had him serve as Palace Attendant together with his two teachers; all held the salary rank of fully two thousand piculs.
proposals.reason: 两师 means Bo's two teachers (Xu Shang and Shi Dan), not two men surnamed Shi.

proposals.before: At that time Xu Shang was Minister of the Lesser Treasury and Shi Dan was superintendent of the household for the heir apparent; the emperor therefore brought Shang and Dan in as grand counselors of the household, Bo was promoted to chief commandant of waters and parks, and together with the two Shi men he served as Palace Attendant, all at salary rank of fully two thousand piculs.
proposals.after: At that time Xu Shang was Minister of the Lesser Treasury and Shi Dan was superintendent of the household for the heir apparent; the emperor therefore brought Shang and Dan in as grand counselors of the household, Bo was promoted to chief commandant of waters and parks, and together with his two teachers he served as Palace Attendant, all at salary rank of fully two thousand piculs.
proposals.reason: 两师 means Bo's two teachers (Xu Shang and Shi Dan), not two men surnamed Shi.

proposals.before: Only Gu Yong once said, "In the Jianhe and Heping era the eminence of the Xu and Ban houses shook the previous court, scorched the four quarters, and their gifts had no measure; they emptied the inner treasury; favor to women reached an extreme that could not be surpassed;
proposals.after: Only Gu Yong once said, "In the Jianshi and Heping era the eminence of the Xu and Ban houses shook the previous court, scorched the four quarters, and their gifts had no measure; they emptied the inner treasury; favor to women reached an extreme that could not be surpassed;
proposals.reason: 建始 is Jianshi, not Jianhe.

proposals.before: Ban Biao, styled Shuipi, studied abroad with his cousin Ban Si while the household enjoyed imperial book grants and deep coffers, drawing classicists from afar so that even Yang Xuan and his father's circle beat a path to their door.
proposals.after: Ban Biao, styled Shuipi, studied abroad with his cousin Ban Si while the household enjoyed imperial book grants and deep coffers, drawing classicists from afar so that even Yang Xiong and his father's circle beat a path to their door.
proposals.reason: 扬子云 is Yang Xiong (Yang Ziyun), not Yang Xuan.

proposals.before: Biao, courtesy name Shuipi, in youth roamed in study with his elder cousin Si; the family possessed books granted by the throne and was ample in wealth, so lovers of antiquity came from distant regions, and from Yang Xuan downward none of his father's associates failed to visit the gate.
proposals.after: Biao, courtesy name Shuipi, in youth roamed in study with his elder cousin Si; the family possessed books granted by the throne and was ample in wealth, so lovers of antiquity came from distant regions, and from Yang Xiong downward none of his father's associates failed to visit the gate.
proposals.reason: 扬子云 is Yang Xiong (Yang Ziyun), not Yang Xuan.

proposals.before: Duanmu Ci's retirement by moral example strengthened Wei; Shen Baoxu's bleeding feet saved Chu from ruin.
proposals.after: Duan Gan Mu's retirement by moral example strengthened Wei; Shen Baoxu's bleeding feet saved Chu from ruin.
proposals.reason: Chinese 木 refers to Duan Gan Mu (段干木), not Confucius's disciple Duanmu Ci.

proposals.before: Langye administrator Gongsun Hong reported disasters to the capital; Grand Minister of Works Zhen Feng sent aides racing to both commanderies to warn officials and people, then impeached Hong for inventing ill omens and Zhi for withholding auspicious responses and obstructing the sage government—both charged as unfilial.
proposals.after: Langye administrator Gongsun Hong reported disasters to the capital; Grand Minister of Works Zhen Feng sent aides racing to both commanderies to warn officials and people, then impeached Hong for inventing ill omens and Zhi for withholding auspicious responses and obstructing the sage government—both charged with heinous crimes contrary to the Way.
proposals.reason: 不道 is a Han legal category for heinous crimes, not unfilial (不孝).

proposals.before: Wei Shou of old guarded his brother, yet the brother turned raider and ruined him.
proposals.after: Wei Shu of old guarded his brother, yet the brother turned raider and ruined him.
proposals.reason: 卫叔 is Wei Shu (Uncle Wei), not Wei Shou.

proposals.before: Think of vertical and horizontal schemers, exiled tongues, Shang Yang's triple trick on Duke Xiao, Li Si's grab at Qin's moment—they rode storm and crisis, gambled on crooked odds, blazed one dawn and burned by dusk; rogues rued it—should an honest man copy them?
proposals.after: Think of vertical and horizontal schemers, exiled tongues, Shang Yang's triple trick on Duke Xiao, Li Si's seize of the moment to corner the First Emperor—they rode storm and crisis, gambled on crooked odds, blazed one dawn and burned by dusk; rogues rued it—should an honest man copy them?
proposals.reason: Chinese 要始皇 names the First Emperor; idiomatic 'Qin's moment' drops that referent.

proposals.before: Gao Yao advised Yu, Jizi counseled Zhou—their speech reached kings, their plans matched the spirits;
proposals.after: Gao Yao advised Shun, Jizi counseled Zhou—their speech reached kings, their plans matched the spirits;
proposals.reason: Chinese 虞 is Shun's polity/title, not 禹 (Yu); rendering it as Yu confuses the referent.

proposals.before: Formerly Gao Yao counseled Yu, Jizi was questioned in Zhou—their words penetrated emperors and kings, their plans matched sages and spirits;
proposals.after: Formerly Gao Yao counseled Shun, Jizi was questioned in Zhou—their words penetrated emperors and kings, their plans matched sages and spirits;
proposals.reason: Chinese 虞 denotes Shun, not Yu the Great.

proposals.before: Fu Yue rose from a cliff dream, Lü Wang from the Wei shallows, Ning Qi from a roadside song, Zhang Liang from a book at dawn—they waited Heaven's nod, not rhetoric, and so built lasting deeds.
proposals.after: Fu Yue rose from a cliff dream, Lü Wang from the Wei shallows, Ning Qi from a roadside song, Zhang Liang received a book at Pi and Yi—they waited Heaven's nod, not rhetoric, and so built lasting deeds.
proposals.reason: Chinese 邳沂 is a place-name pair, not 'dawn'.

proposals.before: Think of Yi and Shu on Shouyang, Hui in a low post, Yan with his single meal, Confucius closing the Spring and Autumn at the western hunt—their names shook heaven and earth; they are our true exemplars.
proposals.after: Think of Yi on Shouyang, Hui in a low post, Yan with his single meal, Confucius closing the Spring and Autumn at the western hunt—their names shook heaven and earth; they are our true exemplars.
proposals.reason: Chinese has only 夷 at Shouyang; 叔/Shu is not in the source and invents a second person.

proposals.before: Or again there were those who set pure conduct on Shouyang, Hui who lowered his will to a humbling office, Yan who took joy in a single basket and gourd, Confucius who finished his classic at the western hunt—their fame filled the gulf between Heaven and abyss; they are true models for our kind.
proposals.after: Or again there was Yi who set pure conduct on Shouyang, Hui who lowered his will to a humbling office, Yan who took joy in a single basket and gourd, Confucius who finished his classic at the western hunt—their fame filled the gulf between Heaven and abyss; they are true models for our kind.
proposals.reason: Chinese names 夷 explicitly; the literal omits that personal name.

proposals.before: Bian Que and Hua Tuo wield the needle with spirit, while Yi Dun and Zhuo Sang calculate gain across the boundless market.
proposals.after: He and Bian Que wield the needle with spirit, while Yan and Sang calculate gain across the boundless market.
proposals.reason: Chinese 龢、鵲 are He and Que (Bian Que), not Bian Que and Hua Tuo; 研、桑 are Yan and Sang, not Yi Dun and Zhuo Sang.

proposals.before: Bian Que and Hua Tuo bring essence to needle and stone, Yi Dun and Zhuo Sang reckon profit in the boundless.
proposals.after: He and Bian Que bring essence to needle and stone, Yan and Sang reckon profit in the boundless.
proposals.reason: Same mismatch as idiomatic: 龢、鵲 and 研、桑 are mistranslated.

decisions.reason: Focus unit 與兩師並侍中 follows 許商 and 師丹 as Bo's instructors; 兩師 means those two teachers, not two men surnamed Shi. The proposed idiomatic repair restores that sense without inventing content.
The same clause 與兩師並侍中 names Bo's two teachers Xu Shang and Shi Dan; rendering 兩師 as "the two Shi men" misreads 師 as a shared surname. The literal repair is accurate.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 引商、丹入為光祿大夫，伯遷水衡都尉，與兩師並侍中

decisions.reason: Focus unit 建始、河平之際 uses the era name 建始 (Jianshi); Jianhe would be 建和. Correcting only that era name matches the Chinese and the idiomatic already on the same unit.
Focus unit 父黨揚子雲以下 names Yang Xiong by courtesy name 子雲; Yang Xuan invents a different person. The proposed idiomatic replacement is correct.
The same 揚子雲 is Yang Xiong (Ziyun), not Yang Xuan. The literal repair restores the attested personal name.

decisions.after: Duan Ganmu's retirement by moral example strengthened Wei; Shen Baoxu's bleeding feet saved Chu from ruin.
decisions.reason: 木偃息以蕃魏兮 alludes to Duan Ganmu (段干木), whose withdrawal strengthened Wei; Duanmu Ci does not fit. The worker found the correct person, but the corpus convention writes the name as Duan Ganmu.

decisions.after: Langye administrator Gongsun Hong reported disasters to the capital; Grand Minister of Works Zhen Feng sent aides racing to both commanderies to warn officials and people, then impeached Hong for inventing ill omens and Zhi for withholding auspicious responses and obstructing the sage government—both accused of capital crimes.
decisions.reason: The unit ends 皆不道; 不道 is a grave Han legal category, not 不孝 'unfilial.' 'Capital crimes' conveys the legal force without the worker's cumbersome gloss inside the sentence.

decisions.after: Shu Wu once guarded Wei for his elder brother, yet was slain as an enemy when that brother returned.
decisions.reason: The allusion is not to a person named Wei Shu. 衛叔 abbreviates Shu Wu of Wei, who guarded the state for his elder brother, Duke Cheng; 昆 means that elder brother. The worker caught the bad reading Shou but did not resolve the historical allusion.

decisions.after: Think of the vertical and horizontal strategists and the exiles who peddled their arguments: Shang Yang used three techniques to insinuate himself with Duke Xiao, and Li Si exploited the needs of the age to win over the First Emperor. They caught the winds of opportunity and rode the turmoil of their times, seizing crooked chances to gain a day's wealth and honor. Glorious in the morning, by evening they were ruined; their good fortune did not last a moment, while their calamities burdened the age. Even evil men came to regret this path. How much less should a good man rely on it?
decisions.reason: 李斯奮時務而要始皇 explicitly names the First Emperor and describes Li Si using the demands of the age to win him over. The worker found the omitted referent, but both its proposal and the prior compressed English obscured much of the passage.
Focus unit 咎繇謨虞 uses 虞 for Shun (有虞), not 禹 Yu the Great. Gao Yao advising Shun is the standard pairing; the repair removes the false referent.
The same 謨虞 denotes counseling Shun; rendering 虞 as Yu the Great confuses distinct graphs and persons. The literal repair is correct.

decisions.after: Fu Yue was revealed in a dream at Fuyan; Lü Wang's omen stirred on the banks of the Wei; Ning Qi's song rang out at the crossroads; and Zhang Liang received the book at the bridge at Xiapi. All awaited their appointed time and communed in spirit, relying on more than words; thus they could devise certain strategies and achieve immeasurable merit.
decisions.reason: 漢良受書於邳沂 refers to Zhang Liang receiving the book from the old man at the bridge at Xiapi; 沂 is glossed as a water bank and is not a second place named Yi. The worker correctly rejected 'at dawn' but misread 邳沂 as a place-name pair.

decisions.after: Then there were Boyi, who upheld his conduct on Mount Shouyang; Liuxia Hui, who humbled his aspirations to take a dishonorable post; Yan Hui, who delighted in his basket of rice and gourd of water; and Confucius, who brought his classic to an end with the hunt in the west. Their fame fills the space between heaven and the abyss; they are truly exemplars for men such as us.
decisions.reason: 夷 is an abbreviated reference to Boyi, not an individual named Yi, while the source names no separate Shuqi here. The worker removed the invented second person but left the remaining allusions too cryptic for English readers.

decisions.after: Or again, Boyi upheld his conduct on Shouyang; Liuxia Hui lowered his aspirations to accept a humiliating post; Yan Hui delighted in a basket of rice and a gourd of water; and Confucius ended his classic with the western hunt. Their fame fills the space between heaven and the abyss; they are true models for men such as us.
decisions.reason: The Chinese explicitly names 夷, an abbreviation for Boyi. The prior literal omitted him, while the worker's bare 'Yi' failed to identify the allusion and left the other abbreviated names opaque.

decisions.after: Yi He and Bian Que mastered the needle and stone probe; Ji Yan and Sang Hongyang's financial calculations knew no bounds.
decisions.reason: 龢、鵲 are Yi He and Bian Que, while 研、桑 are Ji Yan and Sang Hongyang. The worker correctly rejected Hua Tuo, Yi Dun, and Zhuo Sang, but its one-syllable labels were not useful identifications in English.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 龢、鵲發精於鍼石，研、桑心計於無垠

decisions.after: Yi He and Bian Que brought their finest skill to needles and stone probes; Ji Yan and Sang Hongyang applied mental calculation without limit.
decisions.reason: The same abbreviations identify Yi He, Bian Que, Ji Yan, and Sang Hongyang. Expanding the names avoids replacing one set of misleading names with four ambiguous syllables.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 龢、鵲發精於鍼石，研、桑心計於無垠

claimRetractions.reason: 昆 is a kinship term meaning elder brother, not the personal name Kun. The allusion identifies the referent as Duke Cheng of Wei.

sourceWitness.citation: s0174; Wen Xuan commentary to You Tong Fu on Wikisource

claimRevisions.reason: Accepted repair of 揚子雲 shows the English personal name Yang Xuan was a mistranslation; the correct name is Yang Xiong.
The advancing repair of 木偃息以蕃魏兮 shows Duanmu Ci was created by the bad translation; the allusion is to Duan Ganmu.
The advancing repair resolves 衛叔 as Shu Wu of Wei, not a personal name Wei Shou or Wei Shu.
The advancing repair confirms 虞 here denotes Shun rather than Yu the Great, so the personal-name claim for Shun should be explicit rather than uncertain.
昆 means elder brother; the Shu Wu allusion identifies that brother as Duke Cheng of Wei.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 昔衛叔之御昆兮，昆為寇而喪予

claimRevisions.reason: 夷 on Mount Shouyang is the conventional abbreviation for Boyi, not a personal name Yi.
龢 in the paired expression 龢鵲 abbreviates the physician Yi He.
研 in 研桑 abbreviates Ji Yan, the adviser also known as Ji Ran.
Ji Yan is invoked for financial strategy, but was an adviser and economic thinker rather than a merchant.
桑 in 研桑 abbreviates the Han financial official Sang Hongyang.
Sang Hongyang was a Han financial official; the allusion praises his calculation, not private mercantile activity.

proposals.before: The Bans' ancestors shared the same clan name as Chu and were descended from Grand Governor Ziwen.
proposals.after: The Bans' ancestors shared the same clan name as Chu and were descended from Chief Minister Ziwen.
proposals.reason: 令尹 is the Chu chief-minister title Lingyin, not Grand Governor.

proposals.before: The sovereign sent Attendant-in-chamber and Colonel of the Gentlemen Zhonglang Wang Shun, riding post-horses, to replace Bo in escorting the Chanyu, and with him presented the edict, seal, and cord, forthwith appointing Bo as governor of Dingxiang.
proposals.after: The sovereign sent the Palace Attendant and Gentlemen General Wang Shun, riding post-horses, to replace Bo in escorting the Chanyu, and with him presented the edict, seal, and cord, forthwith appointing Bo as governor of Dingxiang.
proposals.reason: 侍中中郎將 is Palace Attendant and zhonglang general; the literal fuses the office unnaturally.

proposals.before: After Empress Xu fell, Lady Ban withdrew to serve the Dowager in the eastern palace, a maid named Li Ping rose to an honored lady, and Zhao Feiyan took the empress's seal; Ban Bo promptly claimed serious illness.
proposals.after: After Empress Xu fell, Lady Ban withdrew to serve in the eastern palace, a maid named Li Ping rose to an honored lady, and Zhao Feiyan took the empress's seal; Ban Bo promptly claimed serious illness.
proposals.reason: Chinese 供養東宮 names the Eastern Palace, not an explicit Dowager; English inserts an unstated person.

proposals.before: She insisted that Marquis Zhang Fang of Fuping be ordered back to his estate for the time being."
proposals.after: She insisted that the Marquis of Fuping be ordered back to his estate for the time being."
proposals.reason: Chinese names only 富平侯 here; Zhang Fang is not in this unit and should not be invented in the idiomatic English.

proposals.before: At that time Xu Shang was Minister of the Lesser Treasury and Shi Dan was superintendent of the household for the heir apparent; the emperor therefore brought Shang and Dan in as grand counselors of the household, Bo was promoted to chief commandant of waters and parks, and together with his two teachers he served as Palace Attendant, all at salary rank of fully two thousand piculs.
proposals.after: At that time Xu Shang was Minister of the Lesser Treasury and Shi Dan was Chamberlain for Attendants; the emperor therefore brought Shang and Dan in as grand counselors of the household, Bo was promoted to chief commandant of waters and parks, and together with his two teachers he served as Palace Attendant, all at salary rank of fully two thousand piculs.
proposals.reason: 光祿勳 is Chamberlain for Attendants / superintendent of the imperial household, not specifically of the heir apparent.

proposals.before: Because palace books were still withheld from the public, the Prince of Dongping's request, as imperial uncle, for Sima Qian's histories and the masters' treatises was blocked by the regent's office.
proposals.after: Because palace books were still withheld from the public, the Prince of Dongping's request, as imperial uncle, for Sima Qian's histories and the masters' treatises was refused when the Grand General reported against it.
proposals.reason: Chinese 大將軍白不許 attributes the refusal to the Grand General's report, not a generic regent's office.

proposals.before: In youth Wang Mang sat among the brothers Zhi as a friend, honoring You as an elder and treating Zhi as a junior.
proposals.after: In youth Wang Mang sat in the same rank as Zhi and his brothers as a friend, honoring You as an elder brother and treating Zhi as a younger brother.
proposals.reason: 穉兄弟 means Zhi and his brothers, not 'brothers Zhi'; the kinship verbs are elder-brother / younger-brother treatment.

proposals.before: He likened his cousin to the fool who went to Handan to learn a new gait.
proposals.after: Formerly there was one who learned to walk in Handan.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic invents the cousin-likening frame and 'fool'; Chinese only states there was formerly one who learned walking in Handan.

proposals.before: Shuipi only after the Way of the sages would then devote his whole heart.
proposals.after: Shuipi devoted his whole heart only to the Way of the sages.
proposals.reason: Literal English is ungrammatical and obscures that Ban Biao reserved full devotion for the sages' Way alone.

proposals.before: Think of Xin, Bu, Xiang Yu, or even Wang Mang, who briefly seized power yet ended in the pot or on the block; petty upstarts far beneath them have even less business eyeing the throne.
proposals.after: Think of Xin and Bu, Liang and Ji, or even Wang Mang, who briefly seized power yet ended in the pot or on the block; petty upstarts far beneath them have even less business eyeing the throne.
proposals.reason: Chinese pairs 梁、籍 (Xiang Liang and Xiang Ji/Yu); idiomatic collapses both into Xiang Yu and drops Liang.

proposals.before: Wang Ling's mother likewise saw that Xiang Yu would fall and Han would rise.
proposals.after: Wang Ling's mother likewise saw that the Xiang clan would fall and the Liu house would rise.
proposals.reason: Chinese has 項氏 and 劉氏 (clans/houses), not the personal name Xiang Yu or bare Han.

proposals.before: Wake to that lesson, shun Xin and Bu's ambition, laugh off the deer hunt, respect Heaven's chosen vessel, and you may pass fortune to your heirs instead of becoming a jest to history's mothers.
proposals.after: If heroes truly awaken in fear of such omens, take to heart the clear portions of Ling and Ying, cut off the covetous glances of Xin and Bu, reject blind talk of chasing the deer, recognize that the divine vessel has its destined recipient, and avoid becoming a laugh for the two mothers, then blessing will flow to their descendants and Heaven's stipend will last.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English omits Ling and Ying (陵、嬰) and collapses the two-mothers exemplum that structures the Chinese admonition.

proposals.before: Ni dragged the Way to serve himself and judged Confucius wanting, yet could not rest easy and fell to worldly ruin.
proposals.after: Ni lured Zilu to follow him and said Confucius was still not acceptable; how could he stay tranquil and unwearied? In the end he fell victim to the age's disaster.
proposals.reason: 路 denotes the person Zilu, not the abstract Way; the idiomatic reading invents a philosophical abstraction and loses the interlocutor.

proposals.before: Houji blazed at Gaoxin's court; Chu swelled along the southern rivers;
proposals.after: Li shone bright under Gaoxin; the Mi clan grew mighty on the southern shore;
proposals.reason: 黎 is the ancestral figure Li, not Houji (后稷); 羋 is the Mi clan, not simply the polity Chu.

proposals.before: Gui divined Jiang with a child's stalks, Dan read the tortoise for ritual fate.
proposals.after: Gui nested among the Jiang as a child's milfoil foretold; Dan read the tortoise for ritual fate.
proposals.reason: 巢 means to nest/settle among the Jiang clan, not to divine Jiang; the milfoil (孺筮) is the childhood omen that foretold that settlement.

proposals.before: Gui divined Jiang in a boy's milfoil; Dan reckoned sacrifice from a tortoise in hand.
proposals.after: Gui nested among the Jiang through a boy's milfoil; Dan reckoned sacrifice from a tortoise in hand.
proposals.reason: Same misreading of 巢 as 'divined'; Gui settled among Jiang, with the boy's milfoil as the omen.

proposals.before: What is honored is the sage's ultimate teaching: follow Heaven's nature and cut off false "rightness.
proposals.after: What is honored is the sage's ultimate teaching: follow Heaven's nature and decide what is right.
proposals.reason: Literal English is truncated mid-quote and obscures 斷誼 (decide/judge rightness); repair restores complete sense.

proposals.before: Han Fei finished his essay on persuasion and landed in prison;
proposals.after: When the "Difficulty of Persuasion" was finished, he landed in prison;
proposals.reason: Idiomatic invents the personal name Han Fei absent from this unit; the Chinese continues with silent subject from the prior sentence.

proposals.before: when Lü's price for Qin rose, his house followed him into the grave.
proposals.after: when Qin's bribe had grown costly, his clan too went down into the grave.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic inserts Lü by name where the Chinese has only Qin goods and his clan; aligns closer to the Chinese and the literal.

proposals.before: You judge a golden age by Warring States gossip, like gauging Tai Shan with a desert foot-rule or sounding the deep with ditch water."
proposals.after: Now you, sir, stand in a brilliant age yet discourse on the Warring States, dazzle yourself with hearsay and doubt what your eyes see; you would measure Mount Tai with a Maodun yardstick or fathom the abyss with ditch water."
proposals.reason: Idiomatic collapses 旄敦 to a vague desert foot-rule and drops the address 今子 and the hearsay/eyes contrast present in the Chinese.

decisions.reason: Focus unit has 令尹子文; 令尹 is the Chu chief-minister title (Lingyin), not Grand Governor, so Chief Minister Ziwen is the accurate literal.

decisions.after: The sovereign sent Wang Shun, Palace Attendant and General of the Gentlemen of the Household, galloping by relay to replace Bo in escorting the Chanyu. Wang also bore the imperial edict, seal, and cord that appointed Bo Administrator of Dingxiang on the spot.
decisions.reason: 侍中中郎將 gives Wang Shun's two offices, Palace Attendant and General of the Gentlemen of the Household. The revision preserves both while making the investiture sequence grammatical English.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 上遣侍中中郎將王舜馳傳代伯護單于

decisions.reason: In this context 東宮 denotes the Empress Dowager's establishment. The idiomatic translation legitimately makes that contextual referent explicit and is clearer than merely saying Lady Ban served in a building.
The immediately surrounding passage explicitly identifies the Marquis of Fuping as Zhang Fang. Supplying his name in idiomatic English is accurate contextual clarification, not an invented person.
Focus unit has 師丹為光祿勳; 光祿勳 is Chamberlain for Attendants over the imperial household attendants, not specifically the heir apparent's household.
Focus unit has 大將軍白不許; the refusal is attributed to the Grand General's report that it not be allowed, not to a generic regent's office.

decisions.after: While young, Wang Mang was friendly with Ban Zhi and his brothers, who served alongside him. He treated Ban You as an elder brother and Ban Zhi as a younger one.
decisions.reason: 穉兄弟 means Ban Zhi and his brothers, while 兄事斿 and 弟畜穉 specify how Wang Mang treated Ban You and Ban Zhi. The revision restores those relationships in clear English.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 王莽少與穉兄弟同列友善，兄事斿而弟畜穉

decisions.after: There was once a man who went to Handan to learn a new way of walking.
decisions.reason: The line remains part of Ban Si's direct speech and introduces the Handan parable. The prior idiomatic changes speaker and adds 'fool'; the worker's replacement is accurate but needlessly stiff.
Focus unit has 叔皮唯聖人之道然後盡心焉; the prior literal is ungrammatical, while the proposal correctly restricts full devotion to the sages' Way alone.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 叔皮唯聖人之道然後盡心焉

decisions.after: Though men may seize power in a moment of crisis, even those as brave as Han Xin and Ying Bu, as strong as Xiang Liang and Xiang Yu, or as successful as Wang Mang ended boiled in cauldrons, laid on the block, pickled, or torn apart. How much less should petty men beneath them covertly covet the throne?
decisions.reason: The source distinguishes courage in Han Xin and Ying Bu, strength in Xiang Liang and Xiang Yu, and success in Wang Mang. The revision restores all five people and the sentence's explicit comparison and punishments.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 勇如信、布，彊如梁、籍，成如王莽

decisions.reason: Focus unit has 項氏之必亡，而劉氏之將興; the Chinese names the Xiang and Liu houses/clans, not the personal name Xiang Yu or bare Han.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 項氏之必亡，而劉氏之將興也

decisions.after: Had men of ambition truly awakened to these warnings, looked far, and understood deeply; had they heeded the clear judgment shown in the stories of Wang Ling and Chen Ying, abandoned Han Xin and Ying Bu's ambitions, rejected blind talk of chasing the deer, and recognized that the imperial regalia have a destined recipient; had they not grasped at the unattainable and made themselves a laughingstock to those two mothers, then blessings would have flowed to their descendants and Heaven's bounty endured.
decisions.reason: The prior idiomatic omits most of the argument, but the worker's 'clear portions of Ling and Ying' does not make English sense. The revision identifies the paired exempla, the two mothers, and the warning against coveting the throne.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 收陵、嬰之明分，絕信、布之覬覦……為二母之所咲

decisions.after: Jie Ni invited Zilu to follow him, dismissing Confucius as still unworthy; Zilu would not withdraw from the world's turmoil, and in the end it cost him his life.
decisions.reason: The Wen Xuan commentary identifies 溺 as Jie Ni and 路 as Zilu. It also makes Zilu, who would not avoid the age's disorder and later died violently, the subject of the second half; the worker left both references unclear.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 溺招路以從己兮，謂孔氏猶未可

decisions.after: Li shone as Fire Regulator under Gaoxin, and his Mi descendants grew mighty in the south;
decisions.reason: Commentary identifies Li as Gaoxin's Fire Regulator and the Mi as his descendants who became powerful in Chu. The revision resolves the allusion instead of leaving two unexplained labels.

decisions.after: The Gui clan settled among the Jiang as a divination in Jingzhong's youth had foretold; the Duke of Zhou calculated his dynasty's allotted years from the tortoise shell.
decisions.reason: The commentary identifies the first allusion as Chen Jingzhong's Gui descendants settling in Jiang-ruled Qi after his childhood divination, and 旦 as the Duke of Zhou calculating the dynasty's years. The worker fixed 巢 but left both halves opaque.

decisions.after: Gui dwelt among Jiang through a divination in youth; Dan counted the years by consulting the cracked tortoise shell.
decisions.reason: 巢 means dwell or settle, 孺筮 is the divination made in Jingzhong's youth, 旦 is the Duke of Zhou's personal name, and 祀 here means years. The revision keeps literal labels while correcting both clauses.

decisions.reason: Focus unit has 順天性而斷誼; 斷誼 means decide/judge rightness, and the prior literal is truncated mid-quote and wrongly reads the phrase as cutting off false rightness.

decisions.after: Han Fei completed "The Difficulty of Persuasion," only to be imprisoned;
decisions.reason: The preceding unit explicitly names Han Fei, and idiomatic English may carry that subject across the sentence boundary. The real defects are failing to render 說難 as the essay's title and flattening the contrast.

decisions.after: once Lü Buwei's Qin merchandise had fetched its high price, his clan too sank into the grave.
decisions.reason: The preceding unit explicitly names Lü Buwei and frames his career as trafficking in a state. 秦貨 continues that mercantile metaphor; 'Qin's bribe' is not the sense, while the old wording was unclear.

decisions.after: Now you, sir, live in a glorious age yet discourse on the Warring States, dazzled by hearsay while doubting what you see. You would use a low mound to gauge Mount Tai and a puddle to fathom the abyss. You are nowhere near the mark."
decisions.reason: The proposal restores the address and hearsay contrast but misreads 旄敦 as a Maodun yardstick. It denotes a low mound or small hill, paired here with shallow water as an inadequate standard, and 亦未至也 supplies the closing judgment.
